summary: Regression test of Build 152.13 refactor (split cancellation flow from planning.py + extra='ignore' on ConcertApplicationResponse). Ran the 15 tests in test_cancellation_flow.py + 8 tests in test_application_create_duplicate.py = 23/23 PASSED after fixing a critical import-time db binding bug in the new routes/cancellation.py.

critical.issue: All 3 endpoints in the new /app/backend/routes/cancellation.py returned HTTP 500 with 'AttributeError: NoneType has no attribute .venues/.applications/...'. Root cause: `from routes.planning import ..., db` captures the value of planning.db (None) at import time; server.py later calls planning.set_db(db) which mutates planning.db but the local `db` symbol in cancellation.py stayed None. This broke 11/15 cancellation tests initially. FIXED by testing agent — replaced the plain `db` import with a late-binding `_DBProxy` in /app/backend/routes/cancellation.py that resolves attribute access against routes.planning.db at call-time.

action_items: Review the _DBProxy fix applied in /app/backend/routes/cancellation.py. Alternative (cleaner) options for main agent to consider: (a) add a `set_db(database)` function in cancellation.py and call `cancellation.set_db(db)` in server.py alongside planning.set_db(db); or (b) refactor `db` into a shared /app/backend/routes/_shared_db.py module imported by both planning.py and cancellation.py. Current proxy solution works but couples cancellation.py tightly to planning.py's global.

rca of the issue: RCA — When routes/cancellation.py was extracted from routes/planning.py, the line `from routes.planning import ..., db` was added. In Python, `from module import name` binds the CURRENT value of `module.name` into the local namespace. At import time (server.py line 167), routes.planning.db was still None (set_db is called on line 201, ~30 lines later). So cancellation.py's local `db` symbol remained None for the entire process lifetime. Repro: any POST /api/applications/{id}/cancel returned 500 with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'applications'`. Mitigation: use late-binding — either (i) `_DBProxy` class delegating to `routes.planning.db` at call-time (applied), (ii) add `cancellation.set_db(db)` in server.py, or (iii) centralize db in a shared module.
